purpose: Add six source-exact Charles H. Gabriel observations and illustrations about gospel song plus two poems on faithful service and carrying gospel light.

defaults.author: Charles H. Gabriel
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1915 Rodeheaver Company edition is public domain in the United States; every excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.

entries.title: Sermon and Song, Praise and Prayer
entries.text: it is both sermon and song, praise and prayer, oblivion and remembrance.
entries.slideText: both sermon and song, praise and prayer
entries.sourceLocator: Gospel Songs and Their Writers, page 3
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historic description of how gospel song can unite testimony, praise, prayer, and memory.
entries.reviewNote: This is Gabriel's rhetorical description, not a definition of preaching or worship. Keep the word of Christ primary under the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Text That Is Spiritual and Devotional
entries.text: be spiritual and devotional; it should begin
entries.sourceLocator: Gospel Songs and Their Writers, page 11
entries.recommendedUse: Use within Gabriel's larger sentence as an attributed criterion for the words of a useful gospel song.
entries.reviewNote: The excerpt is intentionally source-exact but grammatically dependent on its context. Evaluate all lyrics by KJV Scripture, not devotional tone alone.

entries.title: Music Written for the Words
entries.text: The music should be written for the words, and not the words for the music
entries.slideText: The music should be written for the words
entries.sourceLocator: Gospel Songs and Their Writers, page 12
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed music-ministry principle emphasizing intelligible, truth-bearing words over tune-first production.
entries.reviewNote: This is a compositional judgment rather than a biblical command. Apply the cited KJV principles of truth and understanding.

entries.title: The Main Thought in the Chorus
entries.text: the main thought is always in the chorus
entries.slideText: the main thought is always in the chorus
entries.sourceLocator: Gospel Songs and Their Writers, page 13
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historical observation about memorable gospel-song structure and repeated central truth.
entries.reviewNote: The statement describes Gabriel's craft practice and is not universal. Repetition must remain truthful, intelligible, and reverent.

entries.title: When the Prison Congregation Sang
entries.text: With few exceptions every man sang
entries.slideText: With few exceptions every man sang
entries.sourceLocator: The Glory Song prison account, page 21
entries.recommendedUse: Use with Gabriel's full attributed account of 1,077 incarcerated men singing together as a restrained prison-ministry illustration.
entries.reviewNote: Do not romanticize incarceration or claim conversion from participation. Preserve human dignity and distinguish emotional response from saving faith.

entries.title: Music, a Right Heart, and Prayer Meeting
entries.text: his soul was full of music and his heart was right. Up to the last he was always found at prayer meeting
entries.slideText: his soul was full of music and his heart was right
entries.sourceLocator: Sketch of T. C. O'Kane, page 26
entries.recommendedUse: Use as Gabriel's attributed remembrance of T. C. O'Kane's music, character, and continuing participation in prayer meeting.
entries.reviewNote: This brief memorial assessment requires biographical corroboration. God alone knows the heart; teach inward truth and steadfast worship from KJV Scripture.

entries.title: May I Be Faithful
entries.text: The talent He gave me, shall I not use it In following His command?
entries.slideText: The talent He gave me, shall I not use it
entries.sourceTitle: The Slighted Stranger and Other Poems
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed two-line poetic question about stewarding God-given ability in obedient service.
entries.reviewNote: This is poetry, not a Scripture quotation. Teach stewardship and the parable's context from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Send the Light
entries.text: Let us not grow weary in the work of love. Send the light. Let us gather jewels for a crown above. Send the light.
entries.slideText: Let us not grow weary in the work of love.
entries.sourceTitle: The Slighted Stranger and Other Poems
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed stanza from Gabriel's missions hymn when teaching perseverance in gospel witness.
entries.reviewNote: The lyric is a poetic application, not KJV wording. Explain biblical light language and perseverance from the cited passages.
